title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Top of page (item d): this completes the 'Scholie' begun on p.75. Earlier on that page a closed disc D has its boundary circle split into an arc α and two arcs β, β̄ meeting at ζ, ζ̄. A map f: D→D satisfies: (1) f maps the open disc onto U = D \ I; (2) f(0)=0, f(ζ)=f(ζ̄)=1, and f is a homeomorphism from α\{ζ,ζ̄} onto ∂D\{1}; (3) f|β and f|β̄ are bijections onto I. I is a segment from 0 to the boundary point 1 that meets ∂D only at 1. The 'welding' homeomorphism is φ = f2^{-1}∘f1 : β→β̄. The Scholie claims a one-to-one correspondence between four kinds of data. (a) rectifiable homeomorphisms φ:[0,1]→[0,1] fixing 0 and 1. (b) rectifiable topological segments I from 0 to 1 in D with I∩∂D={1}. (c) continuous maps f: D→D with properties 1–3. (d), on this page: power series f = Σ a_i z^i with radius of convergence ≥ 1 that extend continuously to D→D with properties 1–3. In modern terms, (c)↔(d) says the boundary extension of the normalized Riemann map onto a slit disc is determined by its Taylor series, since |f| ≤ 1 inside. (b)↔(c) is the Riemann mapping theorem with boundary correspondence (Carathéodory). (a)↔(b) is the conformal welding problem for a slit.

Section B.1 (circled 6): it starts a construction comparing 'complex-analytic Teichmüller groupoids with boundary, with the differential condition' with the Deligne–Mumford boundary. An object is (X, C): a connected compact Riemann surface with boundary of type (g, ν), with C a system of disjoint cutting curves. The boundary carries extra 'differential' data that lets one cap holes canonically; the marginal note refers to the tangent differentials of ∂X'. The construction runs as follows:
- Cut X along C to get X'.
- Glue a holomorphic disc into each boundary circle of X', canonically.
- This gives a compact Riemann surface without boundary, X''. It carries distinguished (punctured) discs.
- The discs coming from the two sides of each curve of C are paired by anti-holomorphic isomorphisms, because the two sides have opposite orientations. The ν discs coming from ∂X stay unpaired.
- Identify the centres of paired discs and puncture or mark the centres of the others. X'' is then the normalization of a Deligne–Mumford stable curve X''' of type (g, ν).

The next page completes this. The anti-isomorphism of each pair of pointed discs gives a non-zero element of T_{x1} ⊗ T_{x2} at each node, which is exactly the plumbing/smoothing parameter of the node. The result is a functor from (groupoid of compact holomorphic curves with boundary of type (g, ν) with holomorphic discs) to (stable algebraic curves of type (g, ν) with 'propagation' data at the nodes and an admissible system of discs at the marked points). The purpose is 'conformal surgery': realizing the Teichmüller/Lego game analytically, with cut surfaces corresponding to points near the Deligne–Mumford boundary decorated by gluing data.
errors: The correspondence (a)↔(b) is not a bijection as stated. Not every homeomorphism φ of [0,1] fixing the endpoints arises as a conformal welding of a slit; existence fails in general (there are non-welding homeomorphisms). The word 'rectifiable' for φ has no clear intrinsic meaning that would characterize the image. Uniqueness of I given φ is fine for rectifiable I: arcs of σ-finite length are removable for continuous functions holomorphic off them (Painlevé/Besicovitch). Existence needs a hypothesis on φ, for example quasisymmetry (Lehto–Virtanen, Pfluger).
Minor: the insertion '|f(z)| ≤ 1 if z ∈ D̊' is a consequence of f mapping into D, not of the radius of convergence. The parenthesis is slightly misplaced logically but harmless.

The 'differential condition' that lets holes be capped canonically is not made precise on this page. One needs an analytic parametrization (or comparable jet data) of each boundary circle. Merely 'tangent differentials of ∂X'' would not determine a holomorphic disc capping in general without more structure.

ideas.what: Correspondence between slit segments in the disc, normalized Riemann maps onto the slit disc with boundary behaviour, their power series, and the welding homeomorphism of the two sides of the slit
ideas.modern_name: Conformal welding (slit case); Carathéodory boundary correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pfluger (1960), Lehto–Virtanen (1960s); Carathéodory for boundary extension

ideas.what: Cutting a bordered Riemann surface along a curve system, canonically capping boundary circles with discs, and obtaining the normalization of a DM stable curve with paired, anti-isomorphically identified discs
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing / sewing description of neighbourhoods of the Deligne–Mumford boundary; Segal-type sewing of surfaces with parametrized boundaries
ideas.usually_credited_to: Plumbing: Fay (1973), Kra, Earle–Marden, Wolpert. Sewing formalism: Segal (1987), Vafa; operadic version: Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov (1995)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower, surgery and the DM compactification qualitatively; this analytic construction does not appear there as far as I know

ideas.what: Non-zero element of T_{x1}⊗T_{x2} at each node produced by the gluing anti-isomorphism (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Smoothing/plumbing parameter of a node; normal bundle of the boundary divisor; twisted real blow-up data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford deformation theory (1969); explicitly as gluing data in Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov, Zwiebach, Kontsevich

missed.claim: Around 1983–84 Grothendieck sets up a functor from bordered Riemann surfaces with cut systems and boundary 'differential' (parametrization) data, glued by anti-isomorphisms of discs, to DM stable curves with node smoothing data in T⊗T and admissible discs at marked points. This is essentially the sewing/plumbing dictionary later central to Segal's axiomatic CFT and to the modular-operad structures on DM spaces (Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov, Zwiebach). Here it is motivated by the Teichmüller tower/Lego game of the Esquisse.
missed.quote: On peut considérer X'' comme la (normalisée de) X''' ... normalisée d'une courbe stable (au sens de Mumford-Deligne)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an independent, Teichmüller-tower-motivated route to the sewing description of the DM boundary. The aim is to make the 'Lego-Teichmüller' surgery of the Esquisse analytic. This link between the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme and the CFT/operadic sewing formalism was only made explicit later, by other people.

missed.claim: The 'condition différentielle' and the 'structure de propagation' at nodes are left undefined. A precise version would be a groupoid equivalence between bordered surfaces with parametrized boundary and stable curves with tangent-tensor data (a real-oriented blow-up of the DM boundary).
missed.quote: groupoïdes de Teichmüller analytiques complexes à bord, avec la condition différentielle
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is closely related to the Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov twisted real blow-up and to the frame/annulus picture of the Teichmüller tower. The archive could show how Grothendieck intended to define the analytic Teichmüller groupoids underlying the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: The welding Scholie is classical complex analysis, and plumbing at nodes was known (Fay, Earle–Marden). Still, the explicit categorical functor from cut bordered surfaces with gluing data to DM stable curves with T⊗T node data, inside the Teichmüller-tower programme, anticipates the Segal/KSV sewing formalism. It is not, to my knowledge, documented as Grothendieck's.
transcription_corrections: The circled '6' before B.1 is a section/item number, not an equation.

The marginal note is uncertain. It seems to read '* via le microscope(?) canonique de ∂X'' or similar, tied to the asterisk after the inserted phrase about tangent differentials of ∂X'. The transcription's 'de X'' may be 'de ∂X''.
The line 'comme la ... X''' stable' reads better as: 'On peut considérer X'' comme la (normalisée de) X''', normalisée d'une courbe stable'; the inserted 'X'''' names the stable curve.
